subject: Recap & next steps — inference affordability and pilot sizing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Chapman <aiden.chapman@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: cost profile, constraints, and pilot options

Aiden — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I kept this short and focused on the cost/TCO levers you asked about.

What we heard (pain points)
- Production prompt volume expected: ~200M tokens/month (mix of short chat and longer generated receipts).
- Tight budget ceiling: procurement indicated ~$25k/month for the pilot period.
- Latency expectations: 95th percentile <250ms for the user-facing chat flows.
- Security: data residency in us-east, SOC2 evidence required (we can share).

Goals you stated
- Validate user experience before wider rollout (pilot ~4–6 weeks).
- Demonstrate unit cost < $0.00012/token for generation portion after optimizations.
- Keep engineering ops changes minimal (prefer Redwood-managed routing with model variants).

Cost / TCO levers we recommend for this workload
- Batching: enabling request batching at the SDK level should reduce per-token spend by ~30–60% depending on concurrency and latency SLOs.
- KV/prefix caching: many receipts share recurring templates — we can cache prefixes to reduce repeated decoding cost (expected 15–25% token reduction on generation calls).
- Quantized model variant: a 4-bit quantized variant is compatible and will reduce GPU footprint by ~40% (with small quality delta on longer completion).
- Routing policy: route low-cost inference (non-SLO critical) to a cheaper model variant; keep user-critical flows on the lower-latency variant.

Initial pilot sizing (proposal)
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week integration + 4-week live traffic).
- Provisioning: Dedicated small pool with burst enabled; target 8–10 token QPS at 95th percentile to meet latency.
- Budget ask: we can run the pilot within ~$20–25k/mo if batching & cache are enabled from day one.

Attachments: I attached a one-page pilot template and a simple TCO model (tco_token_model.xlsx) with the above assumptions.

Next steps (short list)
1) You: confirm the pilot budget band ($20–25k/mo) and pilot start window (you mentioned mid-July).
2) Redwood: we will produce a pilot SOW draft + cost model by Monday and share SOC2 artifacts.
3) Tech sync: schedule 60m integration call (provisioning + SDK changes) with your eng and our solutions engineer (Diego) — suggested window next Tue/Wed.

If that matches your read, I’ll start the SOW draft and loop in procurement docs.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Aiden Chapman <aiden.chapman@ledgerly.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ledgerly.com
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: cost profile, constraints, and pilot options

Jonas — thanks for the clear write-up. This aligns well. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 200M token estimate is our current best-case (peak expected if we roll to 10% of users). For the pilot phase we expect ~40–60M tokens total (lower traffic).
- Procurement confirmed the $25k/mo upper bound for the pilot (finance prefers to stay under $22k but we can stretch to $25k if we get clear ROI checkpoints).
- Latency: 250ms at 95th is acceptable for now; product would prefer <200ms but understands tradeoffs.
- SOC2 artifacts: please send the SOC2 Type II report and any redacted architecture diagrams we can pass to security.

We’re good to proceed with the integration call next Wed (June 18) afternoon PST. I’ll invite engineering and procurement to that meeting.

Appreciate it — Aiden
Aiden Chapman
Head of Product, Ledgerly
aiden.chapman@ledgerly.com

Jonas — reviewed the model quickly. A few notes and confirmations:

- GPU profile: for the target latency and token mix I recommend an A10x (quantized variant) for the pilot; cost estimate in the workbook updated (tab "infra") — should keep us within $18–22k/mo assuming batching is enabled.
- Batching: expect ~2.5–4x effective throughput improvement on short chat prompts if you enable an SDK-side batching window of 20–40ms. That’s what drives the biggest delta.
- Caching: we can enable prefix cache for receipts and reduce generation tokens by ~18% on test data; need product to flag which prompts are cache-safe.

I’ll update tco_token_model.xlsx and push to the Drive link. Marissa, I’ll drop a short note in the SOW with the infra assumptions.

Diego
